clue.text: (&4ac.) What a politician can expect from treacherous colleague mad about our feature exposing corruption, etc?

definitions.text: What a politician can expect from treacherous colleague

indicators.note: 'about' here means turned about, so the word for mad is read from its end

blocks.note: bats is slang for crazy
In the Back is Private Eye's investigative section on corruption

explanation.surface: A satirical magazine expects colleagues to turn on politicians, and plugs its own exposé column.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Our' is the magazine speaking: Private Eye, where this puzzle appears, runs a column called In the Back.
explanation.definitionFit: A stab in the back is a betrayal by a supposed friend, the classic fate of a party leader.

clue.text: Earner's allowance put strain on massage parlour business?

blocks.note: to tax is to burden or strain
'relief' is the euphemism for the sexual service some massage parlours offer

explanation.surface: A taxpayer's allowance is linked, scandalously, to a seedy massage parlour's trade.
explanation.definitionFit: Tax relief is a portion of income exempted from tax, an allowance granted to earners.

clue.text: Fight in which Queen starts to undo equerry's corsage

indicators.note: 'in which' says the following letters sit inside the word for a fight
'starts to' asks for the opening letter of each of the following words

blocks.note: a bout is a boxing match
Q is the standard abbreviation for queen
initial letters of the two words

explanation.surface: A royal servant's flowers come undone in a scuffle with the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is a link meaning 'is'; an equerry is an officer attending the royal family.
explanation.definitionFit: A corsage is a small bunch of flowers worn on clothing, so a bouquet is a fair, loose synonym.

clue.text: see 1ac
Fancy Clegg's no. 2? That's as good as it gets

definitions.text: That's as good as it gets

indicators.note: 'number two' points to the second letter of the name before it

blocks.note: a fancy is a notion
second letter of the surname

explanation.surface: A sneer at Nick Clegg's deputy, the Liberal Democrats' second-in-command, as the best one can hope for.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No. 2' reads as Clegg's deputy, but it means his name's second letter. Nick Clegg led the Liberal Democrats in the 2010 coalition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something ideal is perfect, meaning nothing better is possible.

clue.text: Gnome suppressing writer's leader? Jerk!

indicators.note: to suppress is to hold something down within, so one word swallows the other
a leader comes first, so only the opening letter is wanted

blocks.note: a titch is a tiny person, as a gnome is
first letter

explanation.surface: Lord Gnome, the magazine's fictional proprietor, gags a contributor, and is called a jerk.
explanation.walkthrough: Lord Gnome is Private Eye's mock owner; here gnome is just a small person, a titch in British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: A twitch is a sudden involuntary jerk of a muscle.

clue.text: Dear old penis "enhanced" with vitamin extract sources

indicators.note: an 'enhanced' body part has been reshaped, so these letters are rearranged
a source is where something starts, so first letters are taken

blocks.note: ex- means former
taken as written before rearranging
first letters of each word

explanation.surface: A spam-email boast: an ageing member boosted with vitamin supplements.
explanation.definitionFit: Dear in the sense of costly; something expensive costs a lot of money.

clue.text: Welcome Bill Clinton's first two touches on excellent Monica's top

indicators.note: asks for the opening pair of letters of the name
the top of a word in a down clue is its first letter

blocks.note: AC, short for account, is a bill
first two letters of the name
A1 means excellent, written with I for the 1
first letter

explanation.surface: Bill Clinton's first moves on Monica Lewinsky, told as an innuendo about her top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill Clinton' looks like one name, but Bill is the account. A1 is written AI here, a common crossword licence.
explanation.definitionFit: To acclaim is to greet with enthusiastic approval, a warm welcome.

clue.text: Sink quite low for that knighthood?

definitions.text: Sink quite low for that knighthood?

blocks.clueFragment: Sink quite low for that knighthood?
blocks.note: surface: someone stooping to dishonourable depths to win an honour
setter's reading: literally lower oneself onto one knee, as in the dubbing ceremony

explanation.walkthrough: 'Sink quite low' sounds like moral corruption in chasing honours; literally it is the posture taken when the monarch's sword touches your shoulder.
explanation.definitionFit: A knight is dubbed while resting on one knee before the sovereign, so that lowering is literal.

clue.text: Shagging tip: move head to fifth position – pardon?

indicators.note: an instruction to shift the leading letter four places along, a controlled rearrangement

blocks.note: shagging is British slang for having sex
a cue is a hint, a tip

explanation.surface: Sex advice on a new position, met with a startled 'pardon?'.
explanation.walkthrough: The first letter is moved from first to fifth place in the joined words.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Excuse me?' and 'pardon?' are both polite requests for something to be repeated; also both verbs meaning forgive.

clue.text: Sportingly put your balls here, being no loser

blocks.note: first meaning: in snooker or pool, balls are potted into a pocket
second meaning: having made money from a deal

explanation.surface: Smutty advice on where to stow one's balls, from someone who never loses.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in pocket means having gained money, the opposite of being out of pocket.

clue.text: Politician about to get a booze dispenser

blocks.note: re means about, concerning
a publican runs a pub and serves drink

explanation.surface: A politician wangles a job running a bar.
explanation.definitionFit: A Republican is a member of the US party, or anyone opposing monarchy: a political figure.

clue.text: Twat dumping wife for associate

indicators.note: dumping gets rid of something, so a letter is dropped

blocks.note: a wally is British slang for a fool
W is the abbreviation for wife

explanation.surface: An idiot leaves his wife for a colleague.
explanation.definitionFit: An ally is a partner or supporter, someone you associate with.

clue.text: Endlessly mouth disapproval at Cameron's past record?

indicators.note: without its end, the word loses its final letter

blocks.note: to hiss is to voice disapproval
David Cameron is a Tory, i.e. a Conservative

explanation.surface: Jeering at David Cameron's political track record.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cameron's' stands for 'Cameron is', giving his party.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone's history is their previous record, as in a criminal or medical history.

clue.text: Hiatus in MPs' business no one backs – poor situation prolonged by Coalition policies?

definitions.text: poor situation prolonged by Coalition policies?

indicators.note: to back is to go in reverse, so the words are read right to left

blocks.note: parliament's recess is its break from sitting
no, and I for one

explanation.surface: A jibe that while Parliament takes a break, the economy stays stuck because of government policy.
explanation.walkthrough: The Coalition is the 2010 Conservative–Liberal Democrat government, blamed for austerity.
explanation.definitionFit: A recession is an economic downturn, a poor state of affairs.

clue.text: Fast food, the fat dirty old man's habit traditionally

blocks.note: big means fat
a dirty raincoat, or mac, is the stereotypical flasher's garment

explanation.surface: Junk food as the lazy indulgence of a fat lecher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Habit' looks like a vice but is clothing; a mac is a British raincoat.
explanation.definitionFit: The Big Mac is McDonald's burger, the archetypal fast food item.

clue.text: Like coming to break a/c limit in cricket club

indicators.note: breaking the letters apart lets them be reassembled in another order
the rearranged letters are placed inside the club abbreviation

blocks.note: taken as written before rearranging
CC is the abbreviation for cricket club

explanation.surface: Someone getting the air-conditioning cranked up at the cricket club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coming' is sexual innuendo for reaching a climax.
explanation.definitionFit: Climactic describes reaching the peak or climax, which in slang is coming.

clue.text: Wi-Fi: a Scottish housing balls-up

indicators.note: the phrase houses the answer, holding it inside across the words

blocks.note: letters inside the phrase

explanation.surface: A broadband failure in Scottish council housing is a cock-up.
explanation.definitionFit: A balls-up is British slang for a mess or disaster, a complete failure.

clue.text: Political machine has a power over state scumbag

blocks.note: taken as written
P is the symbol for power
PA is Pennsylvania
a rat is a despicable person

explanation.surface: A party machine where a slimy operator holds power over the state.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'over' simply places the earlier letters above the later ones.
explanation.definitionFit: The apparat was the Soviet party's administrative system, so any political machine.

clue.text: Hire female underwear – fail to keep it buttoned

blocks.note: to let is to rent out
a slip is a woman's undergarment

explanation.surface: Renting out lingerie, with a warning to keep one's flies done up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keep it buttoned' means keep your lip buttoned, i.e. stay quiet, though it reads like trousers here.
explanation.definitionFit: To let slip is to reveal a secret by accident, failing to stay silent.

clue.text: Brooks singularly pursuing Murdoch's title "Red top producer"?

blocks.note: The Sun is Rupert Murdoch's tabloid
a burn is a Scottish word for a single brook

explanation.surface: Rebekah Brooks pursuing a Murdoch paper's editorship, the producer of a red-top tabloid.
explanation.walkthrough: Brooks reads as Rebekah Brooks, Sun editor; 'red top' is a British tabloid, here a sunburnt head.
explanation.definitionFit: Sunburn turns the skin red, so it produces a red top of the head or shoulders.

clue.text: Blair's status as a PM: lied about having to enter another country?

indicators.note: 'about' means moved around, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: Tony Blair is a former prime minister
taken as written before rearranging

explanation.surface: A jibe that Blair, having lied over Iraq, might need to flee abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: Being exiled means being banished from home and forced to live in a foreign land.

clue.text: Sex much reduced with near-groin area container?

indicators.note: cut down severely, so only the opening letter stays

blocks.note: first letter
the hip sits next to the groin

explanation.surface: A dwindling sex life and a box worn near the groin, as in a cricket protector.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship carries cargo, so it is a vessel holding things; the question mark flags the loose fit.

clue.text: Contribution from Posh a vocal shambles

indicators.note: a contribution is a part supplied by the words that follow

blocks.note: letters inside the phrase

explanation.surface: Posh Spice's singing contribution being a mess.
explanation.walkthrough: Posh is Victoria Beckham, the Spice Girl.
explanation.definitionFit: Havoc is widespread chaos and disorder, a shambles.

clue.text: Former senior Conservative leaders in thong, Oz-style – many a politician's downfall

indicators.note: leaders are first letters of the words they head
the built letters are placed inside the footwear word

blocks.note: ex- means former
first letters
in Australia a thong is a flip-flop sandal

explanation.surface: A former Tory grandee caught wearing a thong, the stuff of a ministerial downfall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Thong' reads as underwear, but Oz-style means Australian usage, footwear.
explanation.definitionFit: A sex scandal, exposure of sexual misconduct, has ended many political careers.

clue.text: see 29ac.
Balls top? That's really too much!

blocks.note: an over in cricket is a set of six balls
to top someone is slang for killing them

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims that a rude remark about balls goes too far.
explanation.definitionFit: Overkill is excessive action, far more than is needed.

clue.text: Luvvies acting together quite pissed with unknown

indicators.note: drunk letters stagger out of order, so they are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written before rearranging
y is an algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: Theatrical types performing a scene together while drunk with a stranger.
explanation.walkthrough: Luvvies is British slang for gushing actors; Equity is the actors' trade union.
explanation.definitionFit: Equity is the British actors' union, the organised body of performers acting collectively.

clue.text: Very quarrelsome whip together with poodle?

blocks.note: the cat-o'-nine-tails is a whip
and joins things together
a poodle is a breed of dog

explanation.surface: A party whip arguing alongside someone's lapdog, a political 'poodle'.
explanation.walkthrough: Whip and poodle suggest Westminster, a party whip and a toady, but give a lash and a dog.
explanation.definitionFit: A cat-and-dog relationship is one of constant fighting, as cats and dogs supposedly do.

clue.text: (& 25dn.) Lift needed by member carrying little weight (Coalition member)

indicators.note: to carry is to hold, so the small weight unit holds the limb inside it

blocks.note: to lift or nick is to steal
cg is a centigram, a tiny weight
a leg is a limb, or member

explanation.surface: A dig at a minor partner in government carrying little weight.
explanation.walkthrough: Nick Clegg led the Liberal Democrats as deputy prime minister in the 2010 Coalition; the surface jibe is that he carried little weight.
explanation.definitionFit: Clegg was the most prominent Liberal Democrat in the Conservative-led coalition government.
